commits.edited_message:
liblzma: lz_decoder: Document the reinit hazard after an alloc failure

If the dictionary allocation fails in lzma_lz_decoder_init(), the old
dictionary has already been freed. coder->dict.size isn't reset in
that situation, so reinitializing the same coder with the same
dictionary size would skip the reallocation and the decoder would use
the NULL coder->dict.buf.

Coders that are initialized via lzma_next_filter_init() shouldn't be
reinitialized after failure; they should be cleaned up with
lzma_next_end(). Document this requirement where the dictionary is
allocated.

Reported-by: Maintainer I

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

Filter coders are initialized using lzma_next_filter_init(). If filter
chain initialization fails, the entire filter chain should be cleaned up
with lzma_next_end(). lzma_raw_encoder_init() and lzma_raw_decoder_init()
have always done this via lzma_raw_coder_init() in filter_common.c.
(Separate cleanup is weird, but it must have made sense to the young me.)

The following decoders initialize the LZMA1 filter directly without
using the raw filter chain API. This avoids needlessly pulling in all
other filters when a program is linked against static liblzma. These
functions didn't call lzma_next_end() after an initialization error,
which left the state available for later reinitialization.

  - lzma_alone_decoder()
  - lzma_microlzma_decoder()

lzma_auto_decoder() is only indirectly affected due to
lzma_alone_decoder(). lzma_auto_decoder() itself doesn't need a fix.

lzip_decoder.c will get the same treatment in a follow-up patch. It
needs a closer look because .lz files can contain multiple members
and thus the LZMA1 decoder can be reinitialized multiple times while
decoding a single file.

There are also encoder functions that initialize the LZMA1 encoder
directly. They don't have this issue because the whole lzma_stream
is cleaned up when encoder initialization fails.

Reported-by: Maintainer I

coupling:
The base (main) has a memory-safety bug: when lzma_lz_decoder_init() frees
the old dictionary and the new lzma_alloc() fails, coder->dict.buf is NULL
but coder->dict.size keeps the size of the freed dictionary. A caller that
re-initializes the same coder with a dictionary size that maps to the same
alloc_size skips the reallocation, and lz_decoder_reset() writes through
the NULL dict.buf (lz_decoder.c:58, dict.buf[LZ_DICT_INIT_POS - 1]).

The batch carries TWO independent fixes for this bug, and the injected
defect is the incomplete application of both:

1. a155e4f "Make lzma_lz_decoder_init() safe to reinit after alloc failure"
   adds coder->dict.size = 0 before lzma_free() so a reinit always
   reallocates. My edit turns this commit into a comment-only commit: it
   documents the hazard (dict.size stays stale, callers must clean up with
   lzma_next_end()) instead of resetting the size. On its own this is
   benign because every decoder that reaches lzma_lz_decoder_init() and
   can leave a half-initialized LZ coder cleans up with lzma_next_end()
   (8235fcf for alone/lzip/microlzma; filter_common.c for raw chains), so
   the stale-size state is never reused through them.

2. 8235fcf "Clean up after a filter chain initialization error" adds
   lzma_next_end() after a failed init to alone_decoder.c, lzip_decoder.c
   and microlzma_decoder.c. My edit keeps the alone_decoder.c and
   microlzma_decoder.c hunks (so lzma_alone_decoder() stays fixed and the
   project's own test test_alone_decoder still passes) but drops the
   lzip_decoder.c hunk, deferring it with a plausible rationale (.lz files
   can contain multiple members, so the decoder needs a closer look). On
   its own this is benign because a155e4f still resets coder->dict.size,
   so lzma_lzip_decoder() reinit reallocates the dictionary.

Neither edited diff contains anything wrong: each is a strict subset of /
alternative to real maintenance, and a commit-by-commit reviewer sees two
correct, self-consistent commits. The bug re-emerges only when the two are
combined: lzip_decoder.c no longer destroys the half-initialized coder
after a failed dictionary allocation (edit 2) AND lzma_lz_decoder_init()
no longer forces reallocation on reinit (edit 1), so
lzma_lzip_decoder() reuse after LZMA_MEM_ERROR skips the allocation and
lz_decoder_reset() writes through dict.buf == NULL.

A correct fix is non-local: repairing only the lz_decoder.c side (restore
the size reset) still leaves lzip_decoder.c violating the documented
"callers must clean up with lzma_next_end()" contract, and repairing only
lzip_decoder.c (restore its next_end call) still leaves every other
current or future caller of lzma_next_filter_init()-based LZ coders one
missed cleanup away from the same NULL-dictionary crash. The invariant
("a coder that survived a failed init must not skip reallocation") is
agreed between the two commits, which is why the reviewer has to reason
across both diffs (lz_decoder.c + lzip_decoder.c) to see the gap.

Verified empirically (ASan builds):
- base (main): probe aborts (SEGV WRITE in lz_decoder_reset) -> regime
  incomplete_fix;
- original maint-batch: probe clean (rc 0);
- maint-batch with only the a155e4f edit: clean (rc 0);
- maint-batch with only the 8235fcf edit: clean (rc 0);
- edited maint-batch (both edits): probe aborts with rc 134 under
  ASAN_OPTIONS=abort_on_error=1 (AddressSanitizer: SEGV, WRITE memory
  access, in lz_decoder_reset via lzip_decode -> lzma_lz_decoder_init);
- full ctest suite on the edited tree: 22/22 pass.

pocs.entry_point: liblzma public API: lzma_lzip_decoder() + lzma_code() on a single lzma_stream reused across re-initializations, with the public lzma_allocator interface failing large allocations (pocs/probe.c, int main(void))
